meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means conflict .

This is the gambler radical. Imagine the 十 on top as a ten-gallon cowboy hat, sitting on the head of a man holding a card in each hand, with tall stacks of casino chips rising from the table in front of him. He's your stereotypical high-stakes gambler. You could also remember this with the components: a gambler holding a cross while playing blackjack, standing on his two legs expectantly, praying to win because he's just gambled those legs on the next card.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means happiness . Don't get it confused with the spicy radical 辛 , they're very similar!
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means long ago .
This looks like a mask , right? Kind of a scary, non-human mask, what with the horns on top and everything, but definitely a mask.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means noon .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means previous .
There's a treasure radical inside this box. What holds treasures? A treasure chest .

You see a slide covered in dirt and use your mouth to clean it off. Then, you announce to everyone that the slide is clean and they can use it safely again. Hints Imagine announcing to all the denizens of the playground that you've licked their slide clean. For some reason, no one seems to be rushing to play on it…
readingMnemonic: After you announce the slide is clean, you take a big swig of Coke ( こく ). The dirty slide left a nasty taste in your mouth, but the Coke is helping to wash it away. Hints Honestly, after that big announcement, you deserve a Coke. Public speaking's hard, so you should treat yourself to a Coke whenever you announce something — regardless of whether you had to lick something gross beforehand.

meaningMnemonic: You ride your scooter through the dirt while carrying a sheep because you're determined to attain something. Greatness? Glory? Everlasting fame? Maybe you'll attain a plural combination of all those things. After all, you are the best sheep-carrying off-road scooterist the world has ever seen. Hints Feel the dirt spatter your face as you zip around off-road trails with your sheep under your arm. You will attain glory! You will attain greatness!
readingMnemonic: After you attain that plural combination of glory, greatness, and fame, you get a tattoo ( たつ ) to celebrate: "world's greatest," in gothic lettering, above a picture of you and your sheep on your scooter. Hints Feel the pain of the tattoo needle as you get this commemorative tattoo. You're getting this tattoo on your forehead, of course, because you want to make sure everyone sees it.

meaningMnemonic: In a dangerous fire , a gambler will always try to bake something before fleeing to safety. It could be his own house on fire, and the gambler would still use the free heat source to get some baking done. Maybe he's gambling that those baked goods will offset the cost of a new home… This kanji also means burn , because that's what happens when you expose something to a lot of heat. Hints Imagine you're the gambler. Feel the heat intensify as your nostrils fill with the smell of baked goods.
readingMnemonic: He used to bake for the Ya nkees ( や ). Baseball cakes, bat baguettes, that kind of thing. A career-ending kitchen injury forced him to retire. That's when he developed a gambling problem. But he still likes to bake whenever the Yankees are on TV. Hints Imagine this guy running around baking in the fire of his home, only this time with a Yankees hat and jersey on. He doesn't bake for them anymore, but he still loves the team.

meaningMnemonic: Your leader from long ago thought to borrow something precious from you. This leader did not return the thing he borrowed, and now he will pay. Hints Think about what precious thing this leader borrowed from you so long ago. What was it? Think about how angry you are about not having the thing returned to you.
readingMnemonic: In your rage, you decide to find this leader, take back what's yours, and in return, borrow the leader's life. So you found him, grabbed him, and threw him into a shack ( しゃく ) — where you "borrow" a few parts of the leader himself, and do other terrible things to him. Hints Come up with all the terrible things you do to this leader in the shack. Hey, it's just a little payback for the borrowing he did.

meaningMnemonic: The bow radical and the bow kanji are exactly the same! Hints Make sure you know those radicals!
readingMnemonic: You have a bow in one hand and in the other... a cu cumber ( きゅう ). You're going to shoot this cucumber with this bow into the salad you're making. Many people don't know this, but this makes your cucumbers taste better. Hints Imagine fitting a cucumber into the string of your bow. Imagine the smell of it as you draw the string back. Mm, take a quick bite, then let it loose.

meaningMnemonic: Nestled in the light of the moon in the grass is a treasure chest that you can see with your brain . You close your eyes, and you can see the spot, but it's kept deep in your brain, and you have to use its power to find it. Hints As you visualize the treasure chest you realize that the moon was your face, the grass your hair, and the treasure chest your brain! It was you all along!
readingMnemonic: If you can unlock the secrets of your brain you'll have powers like No stradamus ( のう ). Nostradamus was able to look inward at his own hidden brain treasure chest and see the future, so maybe you can be like him too. Hints Use your brain like Nostradamus and try to see the future. You see... you see... huh, your brain is just surrounded by kanji.

meaningMnemonic: What do you eat like a machine ? Candy ! Hints Picture your mouth opening and closing really fast and hard as candy on a conveyor belt goes sliding in. Munch, munch, munch, you're a candy machine!
readingMnemonic: This candy in particular is just drops of hardened, clear sugar that looks like 雨 ( あめ ) drops. Hints Picture this kanji rain as it goes into your chomping machine mouth. It tastes like sweet, sugary 雨 . Yum!

meaningMnemonic: In a moon prison , there lies a treasure chest containing a golden chest piece. This mighty chest armor will grant you protection from nearly any attack, because it is imbued with moon magic. Hints Imagine finding this treasure chest and donning the mighty chest armor. Feel the weight of the golden chest piece and the vast protection it grants you.
readingMnemonic: Where is this chest armor from? It's from the moon. Now how would you say that if you were Canadian? It's from the moon, eh ( むね ). Right, this here chest armor is from the moon, eh. Hints If you can remember this kanji's reading and meaning with a Canadian accent, you'll have no problem, eh.

meaningMnemonic: You've got a car , a weapon , and some thread lying around. So of course you decide to connect them all together. Hints Imagine using the thread to fasten the weapon onto your car, creating some kind of monstrosity. Surely this can't be legal?!
readingMnemonic: There's only one reason you've connected all this together: Tuna ( つな ) fishing. Obviously! Hints Your weapon of choice is a harpoon, which is perfect for catching big tuna. We'll just have to hope your car is amphibious, or we might run into some issues. Now let's go catch some tuna!

meaningMnemonic: In your mouth and all the way down to your rib cage there's a sword that's big . But not too big for you to consume . That's why it's in there — you consumed it. Why would you do that? You must be one of those sword-swallowing circus performers. Hints Imagine yourself doing this trick where you put a big sword in your mouth. You say: "Now, for my next trick, I will consume a sword!" Then feel the tickle between your mouth and rib cage, as your esophagus hugs that big sword.
readingMnemonic: This " consume a sword" trick came with a cheap magic kit ( きつ ) you had. Hints It's odd that there would be a "consume a sword" trick in your magic kit. It seems a little dangerous for a kit you can just buy at the store.

meaningMnemonic: The bamboo temple is equal to all of the other non-bamboo temples. Just because it's made of bamboo doesn't make it any less special and spiritual. Hints Picture this bamboo temple compared to some temples made of stone or wood. It's the same size, shape, and it has the same number of worshipers. It's equal in every way.
readingMnemonic: The bamboo temple is also an equal distance away from the other temples in とう きょう . When you look at a map of とうきょう temples, you can measure them out and they'll all be perfectly equal. Hints While many things in とうきょう may not be created equal, the temples are, at least.

meaningMnemonic: A tree that's been sliced up in winter can be used as a flat object counter . Since it's winter, all the leaves have fallen off the tree, so it's easy to cut into slats. These slats can be used as counters for flat objects. Hints What with the snow and wind, winter also tends to knock trees down flat… which is probably why the tree radical on the left looks all flat and squished here. That's another way to remember this kanji is a counter for flat stuff!
readingMnemonic: As you count each counter for flat objects , a bunch of mi ce ( まい ) show up and start climbing all over you. This won't do, so you take two slats and start smashing and flattening all the mice. Now that the mice are flat too, you can also use them as a counter for flat objects. Good job, mice. Hints Now imagine yourself counting with these mice you just smashed. They're freshly dead, so there's not much of a stench yet, but you still feel bad about using dead mice to help you count. Imagine yourself counting with these mice as you try to hold back tears from all the murder you just did.

meaningMnemonic: The death of your heart will cause you to forget all of the most important things. People think memories are kept in your brain, but that's not true. Your heart is where all of your most precious memories are kept, and when it dies, you forget them all. Hints Imagine someone close to you experiencing the death of their heart. They look right at you but they've already started to forget everything. I know this is not a fun thing to imagine, but use that emotion to help you remember this kanji, not forget it.
readingMnemonic: When someone forget s everything they're left with only one thing to do: go bow ling ( ぼう ). Bowling is easy, and there's nothing to forget. You pick up a ball. You drop it. Everything else is automatically taken care of. Hints You know, that's probably why so many old people go bowling. They forgot everything else.

meaningMnemonic: Using flowers to make a lip ring is always going to end in frustration . Hints Have you ever made a daisy chain? Try making a daisy lip ring. Just imagine your frustation as you try to make it small enough to fit through your lip piercing.
readingMnemonic: After some frustration , you made your flower lip ring. Now you look like an Egy ptian  ( いじ ) pharaoh. Because all ancient Egyptian monarchs wore flower lip rings (historical fact)! Hints Imagine yourself dressed as an ancient Egyptian pharaoh, wearing your newly-crafted flower lip ring. Think how classy (or strange) you feel.

meaningMnemonic: You say stuff to a river , giving it instruction . This river is a new river so it needs you to say things, giving it instruction on what to do. Otherwise the river wouldn’t know how to behave. Hints Imagine saying things to this river. What would you say? Flow harder! Babble better! Picture yourself shouting at the river as the water moves along.
readingMnemonic: Actually, you're giving this river instruction in the ancient art of kun g fu ( くん ). Hints The river is soaking up your kung fu instruction like a pro. No one's ever taken your "be water, my friend" instruction and applied it so perfectly before.

meaningMnemonic: If a grain seems extra heavy , you know it's a different kind . Not all type s of grains are the same. So when you feel the heavy type, you know it isn't the same as the light kind. Hints Imagine sorting all the different types of grains by their weight.
readingMnemonic: You sort all of the different kind s and type s by putting them in the right chu tes ( しゅ ). They slide away, probably to some big type-based piles you can't see. Hints Picture the two chutes you use to separate the different types of grains. One has a sign that says "Light Chute" and the other says "Heavy Chute."

meaningMnemonic: You want to share happiness with people so you stamp stool s with the news . Now when people want a report of all the happy things going on, they can just look down before they sit. Hints Stand up and look at the happy news today! It definitely isn't sad or depressing.
readingMnemonic: You research and report the news from ho me ( ほう ). Only after, once all of the news is stamped onto the stools, do you leave your home. Hints Because your reporting is done from home, most of the news is about how your plants are growing. What the cat did this morning. And it certainly isn't the news without the weather!

meaningMnemonic: The paragraph radical and the paragraph kanji are exactly the same! Hints Know your radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: You have to write an entire paragraph about a topic, so you choose coo kies ( く ). Hints Imagine actually getting an assignment to write a paragraph all about cookies. Would you write about your favorite cookies? Your eating methods?

meaningMnemonic: Say it at noon . That's the only time I will allow you to say it. That's the only time I will permit you to say it. Other than that, no saying anything. Noon is your window. Hints Imagine a world where you're not allowed to say anything except for at noon. At that moment, after you've been staring at the clock, waiting for that opportunity, you burst forth with things you want to say. But, once it hits 12:01, you are grabbed and your mouth is covered. You are not permitted to say anything outside of that time.
readingMnemonic: Where do these archaic horrible rules exist? The smaller version of Kyoto, Little Kyo to ( きょ ). Normal Kyoto is just fine. This smaller one is where a group of people went to create their own little town with their own dumb rules. Hints Imagine going to big Kyoto where everything is fine. Then, go to little Kyoto where it's not. Little Kyoto has the short きょ (instead of the long one), and this is how you can remember the difference.

meaningMnemonic: With a lip ring , anything is possible . Having a lip ring grants you the power to conquer any obstacle, achieve any goal. As long as it's a passable lip ring, that is. If it isn't good enough, it isn't possible to be passable. Hints Imagine getting a magical lip ring. First, you have to find a passable one. Then, you have to go through the pain of having your lip pierced. Is it even possible to imagine how painful that would be?!
readingMnemonic: Since anything and everything is possible with your new passable lip ring, you use it to get a new ca r ( か ). You go to the car dealership and ask for a free (passable) car. The manager is impressed with your lip ring and gladly hands over the keys to the latest model of your favorite car. Not bad. Hints It was possible to get this passable car thanks to your lip ring. Hooray!

meaningMnemonic: A religious leader wearing a mask could be either a monk or a priest . You don’t know, their face is covered by a mask! Hints Picture this leader in their mask. Listen to them chant prayers that reverberate throughout the building.
readingMnemonic: This monk or priest is wearing a mask to protect their sou l ( そう ). You aren't a monk or a priest, so they don't want your not-religious-enough eyes to dirty their soul. Hints Imagine the monk/priest's bright, pure soul shining behind the mask. You'll never actually see it, unless you're becoming a monk/priest yourself, and then your soul will need protecting too.

meaningMnemonic: Killing two tree s with a jackhammer is expressly prohibit ed. Don't get me wrong, you can rip up one tree with your jackhammer, but not two. Hints Imagine standing in front of a forest with your jackhammer, staring at a sign with just this kanji on it. Tree plus tree with jackhammer equals prohibited. Hmm.
readingMnemonic: The person who decided to prohibit jackhammering two trees is the Kin g ( きん ) of England. He's the only person who's able to prohibit certain things, so it had to be him. Hints Picture the King angrily covering his ears as his subjects jackhammer trees. He screams and shouts, his crown bouncing on his head, and points at his new sign that prohibits the jackhammering of trees.

meaningMnemonic: Within the blue water, a conflict stirs, but is made quiet by the muffling power of liquid. Under this blue water is a great conflict between two sea monsters, but on the surface it appears peaceful and quiet as the water prevents sound from rising above the surface. Hints Imagine watching this conflict from above the blue water on a boat. You can kind of see the action, but you can't hear a thing.
readingMnemonic: As you watch below the quiet water, every once in a while a sa ber ( せい ) breaches the surface and quietly slices back down. Hints Sabers are sharp, curved, and totally quiet. Great for underwater blue conflicts, and sneaky assassinations.

meaningMnemonic: Under a canopy , there are two person s on the dirt . What do they do there? They sit . The people use the dirt under the canopy as a seat for their butts. Hints Imagine how it feels sitting on dirt. Is it comfortable? Probably not. Maybe you feel a little uneasy about just sitting on plain dirt. Try to recall this feeling whenever you encounter this kanji.
readingMnemonic: Who decided people have to sit like this? The C za r ( ざ ). The Czar wants to be above everyone, so he makes them sit on the dirt under canopies while he goes around on horseback or something, towering over them as they sit. Hints This Czar you met is ruthless and has formally banned all non-sitting activities. Imagine the excruciating pain, the stiffness, the cramping in your legs — all caused by this 24-7 sit-a-thon the Czar has cruelly decreed.

meaningMnemonic: If you have a fire and a helicopter hovering beside it, there's going to be a lot of dirt and smoke billowing around. Mostly smoke, on account of the fire. Now it's in your eyes and mouth. It gets in your lungs and you can't breathe. Why, helicopter, why! Hints Imagine the smoke stopping up your lungs and getting in your eyes. All you know other than the smoke is the sound of the helicopter that's causing it to happen.
readingMnemonic: The smoke is too much and you realize this is the en d ( えん ) for you. You're gonna die here! Hints Imagine choking on the smoke and accepting that this is the end. Boohoo, if only you'd learned more kanji before the end!

meaningMnemonic: The water from a tsunami can create a lot of energy when made into steam . Steam power used to be all the rage back in the day. Steam comes from water, water comes from tsunamis, so logically, tsunamis are a great source of energy. Hints Imagine how much steam a tsunami could create. Hear the steam hissing off of the water and feel the moisture from the steam washing over your body.
readingMnemonic: In order to contain this steam energy and store it for later, you lock it up in a box with a key ( き ). That way the energy can be used at a later time. Provided you don’t lose the key, that is. Hints Steam is very light, so carrying this box of steam energy will be no problem. Picture yourself wandering about with a box of steam in one hand and a key in the other.

meaningMnemonic: On your mouth is a stamp that you tap , strike and slap to create a beat! The stamp looks like a little drum, but you're really just hitting your mouth for fun (the stamp was an excuse to make it seem normal). Hints Put a stamp on your mouth and look in your bathroom mirror. Now tap that stamp and make a fresh new beat the young kids can dance to!
readingMnemonic: When you tap and strike the stamp on your mouth, you make a ta-ta ( たた ) sound. Imagine yourself making a beat with the little stamp drum on your mouth. Now listen... たた ! There! Did you hear it? Hints Picture yourself as a drummer, tapping away on a miniature stamp drum on your mouth. With each tap, you create a lively ta-ta beat!

meaningMnemonic: Into your mouth the leader shot an arrow with an attached hook so that they'd be able to see into your throat . Hints Imagine the arrow with its hook shooting down into your mouth and hooking into your throat. Ouch! Now the leader is peering down in there, but you don't know why.
readingMnemonic: From your throat you hear a voice. Not yours, but one you recognize. It's こう いち ! What's that rascal doing down in your throat? Hints The leader starts to tug こういち out of your throat, but he resists. "No, I like it down here, it's dark and damp." The leader gets angry and pulls harder, which hurts! This is your throat, after all, don't you get a say?!

meaningMnemonic: The rice you feed to a big geoduck can be of any type , kind , or category . It doesn't matter what kind of rice it is, the big geoduck will eat it. Hints Picture this big geoduck shoveling rice down in a flurry of geoduckness. Hear the sloshing and goopy glugging as the geoduck gorges itself on every type of rice.
readingMnemonic: While eating every type and kind of rice from every category , the big geoduck has become even bigger. Its body is rui ned ( るい ). It's painfully obese. This geoduck has eaten itself to ruin. Hints Picture this big, rice-engorged geoduck, too big to move. It's now in a wheel chair and on a rice IV. Imagine its wheelchair squeaking by as it wheezes and groans — ruined by all those types of rice.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami previous ly gave everything in this town a good wash . There are many laundromats in this town, so when the previous tsunami hit, all of the detergent mixed with the water and gave everything a good wash. Hints Imagine this soapy tsunami, washing all the things in town. Hear the soapy waves bubbling with cleanliness as they crash down around you.
readingMnemonic: It wasn't just the town that got a wash , it was the cen taurs ( せん ) too. (Centaurs happen to live in this town.) And being half horse, centaurs have a lot of hair that needs washing. Luckily, the soap tsunami gave them a good wash too. Hints Imagine these centaurs frolicking around in the aftermath of the tsunami previous. It's just like a big bathtub for them. Hear them splashing and neighing in the water.

meaningMnemonic: You want your spirit to be simple so you practice Zen Buddhism . Zen is all about meditating and letting earthly things go. There's nothing more simple for your spirit than being Zen . Hints Try out Zen meditation for a little bit. Look away from your computer or phone or tablet and let your life be simple for a second. Just let it all go and free your spirit from all the noise.
readingMnemonic: The reading for this kanji is Zen ( ぜん ), just like the Zen in Zen Buddhism . Pretty easy to remember, no? Just remember that the reading is the same as the meaning. It’s easy! Hints Without a new reading to learn, you should have time to close your eyes and clear your mind. Zen it out, friend.

meaningMnemonic: If you announce something beforehand you will have advance notice . Advance notice is always nice to give. You'll also see this used as an abbreviation of 予告編 , meaning trailer or preview .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: あのドラマの次回の予告、見た？
sentences.english: Did you see the preview for the next episode of that drama?

sentences.japanese: その映画の予告はYouTubeでよく流れてきます。
sentences.english: The trailer for that movie often pops up on YouTube.

sentences.japanese: トーフグのオフィスに殺人予告が送られてきたんです。
sentences.english: A death threat was sent to Tofugu's office.

meaningMnemonic: When you announce something to a wide audience, you're just throwing your message out there for everyone to hear. This is just a big wide advertisement .
readingMnemonic: Sorry, you only learned the kun'yomi reading with 広 . So, think of it this way when you need to remember this word's meaning: You're advertising something. It's a big advertisement to advertise how terrible a person こう いち is. Come up with some terrible things he's done so that you can imagine this crazy Koichi advertisement you made and ran on national TV.

sentences.japanese: 今朝の朝日新聞の新聞広告、見た？
sentences.english: Did you see the newspaper ad in the Asahi Shimbun this morning?

sentences.japanese: このチョコ、コストコで広告の品としてお安く売られてたんです。
sentences.english: This chocolate was sold at a discount at Costco as a promotional item.

sentences.japanese: 図書館から借りた本に、スーパーの広告が一枚はさまっていました。
sentences.english: In a book I borrowed from the library, there was a grocery store advertisement stuck between the pages.

meaningMnemonic: You know that 笑う is "to laugh." This is the noun version, because the う in 笑う turns to い (so don't confuse this as an adjective). What is the noun version of "to laugh"? It's a laugh .
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 笑う , so just make sure you know that so you can know this as well.

sentences.japanese: 日本ではクリスマスディナーにケンタッキーを食べると言ったら、なぜか笑いが起きました。
sentences.english: Everybody laughed for some reason when I said that people eat KFC for Christmas dinner in Japan.

sentences.japanese: もう自分でも何を笑ってるのか分からないけど、ただ笑いが止まらないんです。
sentences.english: I don't know what I'm laughing at anymore, but I just can't stop laughing.

sentences.japanese: 映画を見て泣くなんて、お前らしくないじゃないか。いつもどの映画のどんなシリアスなシーンにも大笑いしてるのに。
sentences.english: It’s not like you to cry at movies. You always laugh really hard when there are any serious scenes in them.

meaningMnemonic: You know how 守る is "to protect," right? This is like that, but it's the noun version. It's not really "a protection," though it kind of is. What things can you wear to protect you from things like bad luck, demons, and ancient aliens? That would be an amulet or a charm . You'll see these kinds of things sold at temples and such.
readingMnemonic: The reading is like that of 守る , so if you know the reading of that word you should be able to read this one as well.

sentences.japanese: このお守り、どこで買ったの？
sentences.english: Where did you buy this charm?

sentences.japanese: 私はいつも父の写真をお守り代わりにサイフに入れています。
sentences.english: I always keep a picture of my father in my wallet as a talisman.

sentences.japanese: 神様にも相性があるから、たくさんのお守りを同時に付けるのは、良くないんだって。
sentences.english: Apparently, even God has compatibility, so it's not good to wear multiple charms at the same time.

meaningMnemonic: The path of the bow . This is archery .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 先月、弓道を始めたんです。
sentences.english: I took up Kyudo last month.

sentences.japanese: 日本の弓道の弓って、どうしてそんなに強いの？
sentences.english: Why are Japanese bows for kyudo so powerful?

sentences.japanese: 早起きして、弓道部の道場で弓道をしてきました。
sentences.english: I got up early and went to the Kyudo club dojo to do Kyudo.

meaningMnemonic: Black smoke is black smoke . It's also something you should avoid if you can.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 黒煙が見えると思ったら、あそこのマンションで火事だって！
sentences.english: I thought I saw black smoke, and turns out there's a fire at that apartment building over there!

sentences.japanese: 俺は黒煙をモクモク出して走るディーゼル車が好きなんです。
sentences.english: I like diesel cars that run with a cloud of black smoke.

sentences.japanese: 黒煙を上げながら冬の北海道を走るSLは、とてもカッコよかったです。
sentences.english: The steam locomotive billowing black smoke and running through the winter landscape of Hokkaido was really cool.

meaningMnemonic: A borrowing task is just another way to say borrowing . This is also for when you take out a loan . 借用 is a formal word for the borrowing of things like money, facilities, or other goods. You can also use it in a jokingly formal way in everyday conversation though, like ちょっと借用しただけだよ (I just borrowed it for a moment).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ちゃんと借用書を書いてくれるんだったら、お金をかしてもいいよ。
sentences.english: If you write me an IOU, I don't mind loaning you some money.

sentences.japanese: このイラストはトーフグのアヤさんから借用させてもらいました。
sentences.english: This illustration was borrowed from Aya of Tofugu.

sentences.japanese: 英語にはフランス語からの借用語がたくさんありますし、スペイン語にはアラビア語からの借用語が多いんですよ。
sentences.english: English has many loan words from French, and Spanish has many loan words from Arabic.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.
readingMnemonic: Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: All we need to shoot a bow is you 'n' me ( ゆみ ). One person holds the bow, the other fires the arrows. Teamwork makes the dream work. Even for shooting bows. Just you 'n' me.

sentences.japanese: コウイチの弓がどこにも見当たらないんだ。

sentences.japanese: あなたの初恋ってどんな感じだった？
sentences.english: What was it like the first time you fell in love?

sentences.japanese: 初恋の人の名前は…たしか、ミッちゃんだったかな。
sentences.english: My first love's name was...I think...Micchan.

sentences.japanese: おじいちゃん、おじいちゃんが初恋をしたのっていつ？
sentences.english: Grandpa, when was the first time you fell in love?

meaningMnemonic: You know that 枚 is a flat objects counter . So, now we're counting! You have five flat objects .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ステッカーを五枚、オマケに付けておきますね。
sentences.english: I’ll give you five stickers as a bonus too.

sentences.japanese: コピー用紙、あと五枚しかないよ。
sentences.english: There are only five sheets of copy paper left.

sentences.japanese: コンビニに行って、葉書を五枚買いました。
sentences.english: I went to a convenience store and bought five postcards.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well, so this is flat object counter . This counter can be used with various "flat" things, such as clothing items , sheets , paper, stamps, dishes, and more. Notice how they're all kind of flat shaped?
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 日曜日のサッカーの試合のチケットを十枚持っています。
sentences.english: I have ten tickets for the soccer game on Sunday.

sentences.japanese: いつもは朝ご飯は食パン一枚だけです。
sentences.english: My breakfast is usually just one slice of toast.

sentences.japanese: トーフグのステッカーを何枚か買いたいのですが、一枚いくらになりますか？
sentences.english: I’d like to buy some Tofugu stickers. How much would one be?

meaningMnemonic: Stop ! That's prohibition (prohibited)! When something is prohibited and you're forced to stop, that thing is obviously forbidden . If you see this you should probably not do the thing it's telling you not to do.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: この学校では、学生のアルバイトは禁止されています。
sentences.english: Students are not allowed to work part-time at this school.

sentences.japanese: このアパート、たしかペットは禁止だったはずですよ。
sentences.english: I believe pets are not allowed in this apartment.

sentences.japanese: ビエトは手下のヤクザたちに、ギャンブルは禁止だと言い聞かせた。
sentences.english: Viet told his gangsters that gambling was forbidden.

meaningMnemonic: A news report that covers things beforehand (before they happen) is a forecast . For example, a weather forecast is a 天気予報 .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 今日は午後から雨の予報です。
sentences.english: Rain is forecast for this afternoon.

sentences.japanese: 天気予報、チェックした？
sentences.english: Have you checked the weather forecast?

sentences.japanese: お天気お姉さんは、明日から暑くなるって予報してたけどね。
sentences.english: The weather girl said the forecast is calling for hot weather, starting tomorrow.

meaningMnemonic: A friend that you attain is your friend . This is the most common way to say "friend," so learn it if you want to make any!
readingMnemonic: You may have encountered this word before since it's so common, but technically both kanji here are using readings you haven't learned yet, so here's a mnemonic: The friend you're meeting tomo rrow ( とも ) is Dutch ( だち ). You know this because a reminder from your calendar app tells you: "Tomorrow: Dutch friend." Tomorrow, the Dutch friend will come over, and they'll say hallo to you in Dutch — or will they just say hello in a Dutch accent? It's never quite clear to you… What is clear is that tomorrow, the Dutch friend is coming.

sentences.japanese: 彼は私の友達です。
sentences.english: He is my friend.

sentences.japanese: よかったら、私と友達になってくれませんか？
sentences.english: If you don't mind, would you like to be my friend?

sentences.japanese: 友達の友達から聞いたことなんだけど、ビエトってヤクザらしいよ！
sentences.english: I heard from a friend of a friend that Viet is a yakuza!

meaningMnemonic: The silver seat isn't some crazy kingdom where the king sits upon a silver seat. It is a famous place in Tokyo. Perhaps if you read the reading it will become more apparent what the meaning is (since they're the same). This silver seat place is Ginza .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 今は銀座にいます。
sentences.english: I am in Ginza now.

sentences.japanese: 銀座にはバーがたくさんあります。
sentences.english: There are many bars in Ginza.

sentences.japanese: 私の友達は、東京の銀座でホステスをしています。
sentences.english: My friend works as a hostess in Ginza, Tokyo.

meaningMnemonic: A product thing is any type of general goods . It's about as specific as you can get when you're talking about thing s like this.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the kun'yomi readings of the kanji. You've seen those readings before, but the one for 品 ( しな ) is a little tricky, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember: Think of the sheen ( しな ) that new goods have before you buy them. When you bring them home, that sheen is already gone. But then you go back to the store and, wow! All the goods you don't already own have that sheen! Gotta buy them!

sentences.japanese: この時間のスーパーには品物がほとんどありません。
sentences.english: There are almost no goods in the grocery store around this time.

sentences.japanese: そのお店のショーケースにはたくさんの品物がならんでいました。
sentences.english: The store's showcases were filled with many items.

sentences.japanese: すいません、こちらの品物はすでにご予約をいただいている物なんです。
sentences.english: Sorry, this item has already been reserved.

meaningMnemonic: A nicely bake d bird isn't just any bird, it's grilled chicken or roast chicken . You may also know it by its Japanese name: yakitori .
readingMnemonic: The readings are the vocab kun'yomi readings. With 焼き , you can use the reading you learned with the kanji. With 鳥 just remember back to the vocab word, とり . Combine and eat.

sentences.japanese: 今日、焼き鳥食べに行かない？
sentences.english: Do you want to go out for yakitori today?

sentences.japanese: 焼き鳥屋でアルバイトを始めました。
sentences.english: I started working part-time at a yakitori restaurant.

sentences.japanese: 焼き鳥は私の生活に不可欠です。
sentences.english: Grilled chicken is essential for my life.

meaningMnemonic: Nicely bake d meat is grilled meat or yakiniku . Mmm, yum! If you go to Japan look out for 焼肉 places (same meaning and reading). They're pretty tasty, if you're into meat at least.
readingMnemonic: 焼き uses the reading you learned with the kanji. 肉 does too. Put them on the grill and enjoy!

sentences.japanese: 今日は焼き肉が食べたい気分です。
sentences.english: I am in the mood for grilled meat today.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は家族でホットプレートで焼き肉をしました。
sentences.english: Yesterday, my family and I had yakiniku using a hot plate at home.

sentences.japanese: 私が特にイライラするのは、焼き肉をクチャクチャ音を立てて食べる人です。
sentences.english: I find it really irritating when people chew yakiniku loudly.

meaningMnemonic: Remember 荷物 and how it means "baggage" or "luggage." Add a hand to it and you have hand baggage or hand luggage .
readingMnemonic: If you know 荷物 and you know 手 , then you should be able to Voltron the two together into one mega reading.

sentences.japanese: 手荷物の中には、必要なものだけを入れるようにしています。
sentences.english: I try to put only what I need in my hand luggage.

sentences.japanese: フロントで手荷物をあずかってもらえるよ。
sentences.english: You can leave your baggage at the front desk.

sentences.japanese: 手荷物チェックのとこで引っかかっちゃったんだ！
sentences.english: I got stuck at the baggage check!

meaningMnemonic: Happiness is happiness !
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet so here's a mnemonic to help you: If your life is filled with nothing but happiness , every time someone says something to you, all you can do is say, " Sigh, wha t ( さいわ )?" You sigh and say what. Because you're too happy to really listen. You're just sighing all day and not paying attention.

sentences.japanese: 幸いなことに、ちょうど空車のタクシーがやって来ました。
sentences.english: Luckily, an empty taxi just came.

sentences.japanese: お役に立てたようで、幸いです。
sentences.english: I'm happy that I was able to help you.

sentences.japanese: 幸いケガはありませんでした。
sentences.english: Fortunately, there were no injuries.

meaningMnemonic: When you are high er than equal , you are above the very top, you are above everyone. You are high class .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: あなたの国の高等教育について教えてください。
sentences.english: Please tell me about higher education in your country.

sentences.japanese: うちの息子はまだ小学生ですが、すでに高等レベルの数学を勉強しています。
sentences.english: My son is still in elementary school, but he is already studying higher level math.

sentences.japanese: このロボットのプログラミングには、高等な技術が必要です。
sentences.english: Programming this robot requires advanced skills.

meaningMnemonic: You have flat object s but what amount of flat objects? This word is asking that question: " how many flat objects are there?" If this doesn't make sense, think back to words like 何回 or 何年 which ask "how many ____" just like this one.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ベーコンは美味しいから、何枚でも食べれるよ。
sentences.english: Bacon is so tasty that I can eat an unlimited number of strips.

sentences.japanese: チケット、今のところ何枚ぐらい売れたの？
sentences.english: About how many tickets have you sold so far?

sentences.japanese: ワニカニのトレーディングカードって、全部で何枚あるんですか？
sentences.english: How many WaniKani trading cards are there in total?

meaningMnemonic: So we have 書く (to write) plus the kanji for way . Is this pattern starting to look familiar? This means how to write or way of writing .
readingMnemonic: This word uses kun'yomi readings for both kanji. You learned the か reading with 書く , and the かた reading for 方 is the one you learned with other "how-to" words like 読み方 and 使い方 .

sentences.japanese: この漢字の書き方が思い出せません。
sentences.english: I can't remember how to write this kanji.

sentences.japanese: ビジネスメールの書き方を教えてください。
sentences.english: Could you teach me how to write business e-mails?

sentences.japanese: この書き方だと、ちょっと文の意味が分かりにくいんじゃないかな。
sentences.english: I think this way of writing makes it a little difficult to understand the meaning of the sentence.

meaningMnemonic: It's not possible to lack . It is indispensable and essential , so don't lack it!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: メガネは私の生活に不可欠です。
sentences.english: Glasses are an integral part of my life.

sentences.japanese: 日本語がペラペラになるのに不可欠なことは何だと思いますか？
sentences.english: What do you think would be essential to becoming fluent in Japanese?

sentences.japanese: ビーチに行く時は、日焼け止めが不可欠です。
sentences.english: When I go to the beach, sunscreen is essential.

meaningMnemonic: The feeling of news is that it should give you information and data , not fluff.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: その情報、どこ情報？
sentences.english: Where is this information from?

sentences.japanese: まずは情報を整理しましょう。
sentences.english: First, let's organize the information.

sentences.japanese: すみません、情報不足でした。
sentences.english: Sorry, I didn't have enough information.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 説明 means "explanation"? Take that explanation and write it down. Now you have an instruction manual or user guide . This is the booklet or sheet of paper that comes with appliances, electronics, or flat-pack furniture — the thing that explains how to use the product.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 説明書通りにやれば大丈夫ですよ。
sentences.english: Just follow the instructions and you'll be fine.

sentences.japanese: 昨日買ったアイスクリームメーカーに説明書がついていませんでした。
sentences.english: The instructions for the ice cream maker I bought yesterday were missing.

sentences.japanese: 新しいゲームをする時に説明書を読んでから始めるタイプですか。それとも、説明書は読まずにいきなり始めるタイプですか。
sentences.english: When you play a new game, are you the type of person who reads the instructions first or do you start playing without reading them?

meaningMnemonic: When you're in a bind , visiting the bureau may be your only option in the end . You were really hoping to avoid it, but it looks like you'll need to go after all . 結局 is used to talk about the final result after everything is said and done. It often carries the nuance that, despite the various factors leading up to something, things didn't go as expected or the outcome wasn't ideal, like 結局行かなかった ( ultimately , I didn't end up going).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Note the けつ gets changed to けっ as つ s in this situation often do.

sentences.japanese: 結局足りない
sentences.english: to not be enough in the end

sentences.japanese: 結局一人
sentences.english: alone after all

sentences.japanese: 結局自分でやる
sentences.english: to do it oneself in the end

sentences.japanese: 結局負ける
sentences.english: to lose after all

sentences.japanese: 結局、彼は試験に合格しませんでした。
sentences.english: In the end, he didn't pass the exam.

sentences.japanese: そう言えば、彼女とは結局どうなったの？
sentences.english: Speaking of which, what ended up happening with you and her?

sentences.japanese: バレンタインの友チョコを買いに行ったんだけど、結局自分用チョコしか買わなかったわ。
sentences.english: I went to buy some Valentine's chocolates for my friends, but I ultimately ended up just buying some for myself.

meaningMnemonic: Remember 関西 , the Kansai region of Japan? Well, they have their own dialect — the Kansai dialect . 関西弁 can actually refer to any number of local dialects from the Kansai region. There are lots of them (Osaka, Kyoto, and Nara dialects to name a few), all with little differences in pronunciation and vocabulary that separate them from the standard Japanese you'd hear in Tokyo.
readingMnemonic: This reading just combines the vocab 関西 with the kanji reading for 弁 .

sentences.japanese: 私は関西弁がしゃべれます。
sentences.english: I can speak Kansai dialect.

sentences.japanese: それは関西弁のイントネーションではどんな感じになりますか？
sentences.english: What does that sound like in the intonation of Kansai dialect?

sentences.japanese: え、なんで関西弁話せるん？しかもめっちゃコテコテの関西弁やん！
sentences.english: Huh, why can you speak in Kansai dialect? And it's a super thick Kansai dialect at that!

meaningMnemonic: The kind and type is the kind , type , or sort . Basically, if you know the meaning of either of these kanji you'll know the meaning of this word as well, since they all share nicely.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: うちの犬は二種類の薬を飲んでいます。
sentences.english: My dog is on two different medications.

sentences.japanese: 全部で何種類あるの？
sentences.english: How many kinds are there in all?

sentences.japanese: 種類が多すぎて中々決められません。
sentences.english: There are so many kinds that it is hard to decide.

meaningMnemonic: The instruction reading may not make a lot of sense, but you've heard this word before. Jump to the reading and you'll know what the meaning of this word is.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the word 読み (like 読む ) and the reading you learned for 訓 combined, making くんよ み . Sounds familiar? It's that kun'yomi reading you've heard so much about.

sentences.japanese: 漢字には音読みと訓読みがあります。
sentences.english: Kanji characters have both on reading and kun reading.

sentences.japanese: この漢字の訓読みって何だったっけ？
sentences.english: What was the kun'yomi of this kanji?

sentences.japanese: え、これって訓読みだったの？てっきり音読みだと思ってた。
sentences.english: Oh, this is a kun'yomi? I thought it was an on'yomi.

meaningMnemonic: The body part that lives between your throat and your head is your larynx . Otherwise known as the voice box , because your vocal cords live in there.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You learned 頭 's on'yomi reading with 頭部 , but here's a mnemonic in case you forgot: If you really want to get a larynx workout, go to とう きょう . It's loud, it's crowded, and you have to yell the entire time to get people to hear what you have to say. You also know 18 levels of kanji and you really want to shout them all out, which makes your voice box tired (but makes you happy).

sentences.japanese: あの方は耳鼻喉頭科の先生です。
sentences.english: That man is an otolaryngologist.

sentences.japanese: 喉頭ガンは酒やタバコが原因で起こることが多い。
sentences.english: Laryngeal cancer is often caused by alcohol and tobacco.

sentences.japanese: 彼は喉頭手術を受けましたが、声を失い、人工喉頭となりました。
sentences.english: He underwent laryngeal surgery, but lost his voice and was given an artificial larynx.

meaningMnemonic: At least way back in the day, things that teach instructions to people are things that teach a lesson , moral , or teachings . Back in the day, lots of learning was done through storytelling, and storytelling taught lessons and morals, thus, this word.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: いい教訓になりました。
sentences.english: It was a good lesson.

sentences.japanese: この教訓をムダにはしません。
sentences.english: I will not let this lesson be wasted.

sentences.japanese: 今回の教訓を活かして、次回はもっと上手くやれるようにしたいと思います。
sentences.english: I hope to learn from the lessons learned this time and do better next time.

meaningMnemonic: A song you sing to protect your child while they sleep is called a lullaby .
readingMnemonic: The readings for this word are all kun'yomi readings. You haven't learned this reading for 守 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you: When you finish singing a lullaby to your child they always ask for more ( もり ). It doesn't matter how many you sing, they always want at least one more before they will fall asleep.

sentences.japanese: これは日本の子守歌です。
sentences.english: This is a Japanese lullaby.

sentences.japanese: アメリカで一番有名な子守歌は何ですか？
sentences.english: What's the most popular lullaby in America?

sentences.japanese: 子供のころ、母によく歌ってもらった子守歌なんです。
sentences.english: That's a lullaby my mother often sang to me when I was a child.

meaningMnemonic: There's only one person type and that is mankind , otherwise known as humanity , or humankind .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 彼は全人類の希望です。
sentences.english: He is the hope of all mankind.

sentences.japanese: 私たち人類は、日々新しいことを学び、成長します。
sentences.english: We, humanity, learn something new and grow every day.

sentences.japanese: 私、地球にとって、人類は悪だと思うんです。
sentences.english: I believe that humanity is harmful to the Earth.

meaningMnemonic: A person who has " attain ed" is someone who knows much. They are a master or expert , obviously.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 彼はカメラの達人です。
sentences.english: He is a master of the camera.

sentences.japanese: 彼女はウチの会社の達人プログラマーです。
sentences.english: She is a programming guru for our company.

sentences.japanese: ウチの母親の料理は、料理の達人レベルに美味しいです。
sentences.english: My mother's cooking is delicious to the level of a culinary master.

meaningMnemonic: This is a day of the week. You know this because it has 曜日 in it. But what day of the week is it? The " moon " day of the week is Monday . Why? Because "Moon" is pretty much just "Mon," right?
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. The 曜日 part is read just like the word 曜日 , which you already learned, but 月 has two different on'yomi readings, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember which one to use: Monday is the day when a person gets ( げつ ) back to their regular weekday schedule. He or she gets out of bed, gets in the car, gets to work, and gets after that paycheck!

sentences.japanese: 月曜日の朝
sentences.english: Monday morning

sentences.japanese: 月曜日のミーティング
sentences.english: Monday meeting

sentences.japanese: 月曜日のニュース
sentences.english: Monday's news

sentences.japanese: 月曜日にする
sentences.english: to do on Monday, to set for Monday

sentences.japanese: 月曜日に行く
sentences.english: to go on Monday

sentences.japanese: 月曜日に出発する
sentences.english: to depart on Monday

sentences.japanese: 今度の月曜日、仕事の後、飲みに行かない？
sentences.english: Wanna go out for a drink this coming Monday after work?

sentences.japanese: 月曜日は新しい週の始まりです。
sentences.english: Monday is the beginning of a new week.

sentences.japanese: 月曜日はいつも起きるのがツライです。会社に行きたくないんで。
sentences.english: I always have a hard time getting up on Mondays. I don't want to go to work.

meaningMnemonic: News travels down the road by way of a news report . 報道 specifically refers to information put out by news organizations or the press in the form of newspaper articles, radio or television broadcasts, etc. Notice that it's different from 報告 , which is more general and means the reporting of information by anyone.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ウソを報道するな！
sentences.english: Don't report lies!

sentences.japanese: 今回のテロのことは、日本ではどのように報道されていますか？
sentences.english: How will this terrorist attack be reported in Japan?

sentences.japanese: 地元メディアの報道によると、ワニカニのレアトレーディングカードがオークションで一億円で落札されたそうです。
sentences.english: According to local media reports, a rare trading card of WaniKani was sold at auction for one hundred million yen.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of a kanji plus hiragana ending with an う sound, so you can probably guess it's a verb. The kanji itself means wash , and the verb vocab version is… to wash !
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Whenever you need to wash something, you call up your friend Ala ddin ( あら ). Thanks to his genie, washing anything is a breeze. You haven't washed your own dishes, clothes, or car in months now. Honestly, Aladdin's friendship has kind of made you a lazy bum…

meaningMnemonic: A zen temple is just what it sounds like, a zen temple . Sounds nice.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the two words 禅 and 寺 put together. The てら gets changed to でら , though. In terms of when it's pronounced ぜんじ , if you put this word onto the end of the name of a 禅寺 the pronunciation changes to ぜんじ . It makes sense - it's more like a jukugo word that way (not that the original isn't, but you can see the separation of words coming together which gives the hint that it's a kun'yomi combo reading). Anyways, you may need a zen temple to keep your mind pure enough to remember this, but it's a good thing to keep in mind if you can.
